news.headline: Dengue virus can infect immune cells meant to fight disease
news.body: Researchers at the University of Vermont's Robert Larner, M.D. College of Medicine and Upstate Medical University in Syracuse, New York, have discovered that dengue virus can infect and replicate inside memory B cells, immune cells traditionally understood to help protect the body from infection. The findings, published July 20 in the Journal of Virology, reveal a previously unrecognized way the virus may evade immune defenses and point toward new strategies for treating a disease that threatens 40% of the world's population, including parts of the southern United States.

news.headline: Fauci repeatedly invokes the Fifth Amendment in a contentious Senate committee hearing
news.body: Dr. Anthony Fauci will face a contempt of Congress vote in a Senate committee next week after he invoked the Fifth Amendment in a hearing about his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic. In Wednesday's hearing, Fauci declined to answer dozens of questions from senators. The scientist's decision to not testify injected drama into the lingering tensions between Fauci and GOP lawmakers over his handling of the coronavirus pandemic and accusations he lied about its origins, which he denies. Fauci was subpoenaed by Sen. Rand Paul, who led the charge to have the now-retired infectious disease expert testify again. The hearing was part of a campaign to arrest Fauci, spearheaded by some congressional Republicans. Fauci says Paul has an “obvious obsession” with calling for his prosecution.

logs.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the fastest-growing ever, with cases surging above 1,000 and the death toll reaching 600. The outbreak has spread to new provinces including Tshopo and Haut-Uele, and the first case outside Africa has been confirmed in France. Response efforts are hampered by funding shortages, unpaid health workers, and the closure of USAID, while new diagnostic tests and treatment trials offer hope.

logs.summary: As of late July 2026, the DRC's Ebola outbreak has topped 3,200 cases and 1,405 deaths, nearing the record of the country's worst 2018-2020 outbreak. The first person has been vaccinated against the Bundibugyo variant in an Oxford vaccine trial, while healthcare workers continue strikes over unpaid wages, and the UN warns the outbreak is worsening hunger in eastern Congo. Meanwhile, Uganda has officially declared itself Ebola-free after its last patient was discharged in June.

Researchers from a Pennsylvania university deployed snake-like robots to assist international search teams. Meanwhile, collection centers in Texas are overwhelmed with donations, and reports continue to highlight the staggering costs of rebuilding as the focus shifts from rescue to recovery.
Public health experts warn that more than a month after the twin earthquakes, Venezuela faces a critical period to prevent secondary crises from contaminants, as survivors and aid workers battle dust, debris, and unsafe water. The country's weak health services and hazardous waste could trigger fresh health emergencies, with the coming weeks seen as pivotal.
Public health experts warn that the coming weeks are critical to prevent secondary crises from contaminants, as survivors and aid workers battle dust, debris, and unsafe water in earthquake-affected areas. Search dogs from the Santa Paula National Disaster Search Dog Foundation, which trains year-round for such emergencies, were deployed to assist in Venezuela. An 11-year-old miniature poodle named Beyli was rescued alive from earthquake rubble 29 days after the disaster, surviving against the odds. Researchers from a Pennsylvania university deployed snake-like robots to assist international search teams. Meanwhile, collection centers in Texas are overwhelmed with donations, and reports continue to highlight the staggering costs of rebuilding as the focus shifts from rescue to recovery.
Public health experts warn that more than a month after the twin earthquakes, Venezuela faces a critical period to prevent secondary crises from contaminants, as survivors and aid workers battle dust, debris, and unsafe water. The country's weak health services and hazardous waste could trigger fresh health emergencies, with the coming weeks seen as pivotal.
Public health experts warn that the coming weeks are critical to prevent secondary crises from contaminants, as survivors and aid workers battle dust, debris, and unsafe water in earthquake-affected areas. incidents.summary:
New reports indicate over 250,000 people have now been evacuated across France and Spain, with at least one death confirmed in Spain. High winds gusting up to 60 kph are complicating firefighting efforts, and the Tour de France has shortened its final stage due to the emergency.
As of July 25-26, the number of evacuees across France and Spain has risen to over 300,000, with exhausted firefighters battling blazes fueled by high winds. At least one death has been confirmed in Spain, and the Tour de France final stage has been shortened to free up security personnel for firefighting efforts.
A new wildfire broke out in Castellon, Valencia, forcing 15,000 evacuations. As of July 26, France has evacuated about 220,000 people and Spain over 75,000 (with 30,000 ordered to shelter in place), while Bordeaux considered a total evacuation as fires advanced to within 15 kilometers of the city. French President Macron called a crisis cabinet meeting for Monday to address the escalating situation.

logs.summary:
A massive wildfire in central Spain has burned over 32,000 hectares (79,000 acres), becoming one of the country's largest on record, forcing thousands to evacuate. The Spanish government declared a national emergency on July 24 as the blaze continued to rage. Three firefighters died in associated wildfires across Europe, with two in France and one in Italy, while Spain's annual wildfire average was crossed before August.
Spain declared its first-ever national emergency as wildfires near Madrid and Avila forced 20,000 evacuations, while in southwestern France over 60,000 people, including tourists, were evacuated from the Cap Ferret peninsula by boat. Both countries requested assistance from the European Union as the fires, fueled by a marine heatwave and extreme temperatures, burned over 100 square kilometers in France.
The total number of evacuees from wildfires in Spain and France has risen to over 90,000, with 40,000 people ordered to evacuate or shelter in the Madrid region alone. A major wildfire in southern France near Cap Ferret is now reported to be under control, though blazes continue to rage in central Spain. Authorities are deploying novel firefighting methods, including using donkeys to graze flammable vegetation.

logs.summary:
By July 24-25, wildfires in southwestern France and central Spain forced over 200,000 people to evacuate, with France reporting 141,000 evacuees from the Gironde and Landes departments and Spain evacuating 60,000. French President Emmanuel Macron ordered military mobilization as a blaze approached the city of Bordeaux, while Spain's national emergency declaration covered the Madrid region and Avila province. Dozens of firefighters were injured but no deaths were reported.
On July 25, 2026, about 20,000 people were evacuated from towns along the French Atlantic coast as a wildfire spread, while around 197,000 evacuations were ordered in the Gironde and Landes regions. France prepared an A400M aircraft to drop retardant on the Gironde wildfire near Bordeaux, and evacuations also occurred near Madrid in Spain as blazes continued.
By July 25, the total number of evacuees across France and Spain has risen to over 267,000, with France evacuating suburbs of Bordeaux as a massive wildfire shifts toward the city. France deployed a specially adapted A400M cargo aircraft to dump flame retardants on the blaze, and French President Macron stated the country "will rebuild" after the fires. Officials described the Madrid wildfire as the "worst fire in the history of the region" and the final stage of the Tour de France was shortened due to the fires.

logs.summary:
New reports indicate over 250,000 people have now been evacuated across France and Spain, with at least one death confirmed in Spain. High winds gusting up to 60 kph are complicating firefighting efforts, and the Tour de France has shortened its final stage due to the emergency.
As of July 25-26, the number of evacuees across France and Spain has risen to over 300,000, with exhausted firefighters battling blazes fueled by high winds. At least one death has been confirmed in Spain, and the Tour de France final stage has been shortened to free up security personnel for firefighting efforts.
A new wildfire broke out in Castellon, Valencia, forcing 15,000 evacuations. As of July 26, France has evacuated about 220,000 people and Spain over 75,000 (with 30,000 ordered to shelter in place), while Bordeaux considered a total evacuation as fires advanced to within 15 kilometers of the city. French President Macron called a crisis cabinet meeting for Monday to address the escalating situation.

logs.summary:
A wildfire erupted in the historic Fontainebleau forest south of Paris, burning over 2,000 hectares and prompting the evacuation of about 1,000 residents. French authorities arrested two people suspected of deliberately starting the blaze, while hundreds of firefighters and waterbombing aircraft worked to contain the fire as Europe faced another heatwave.

The wildfires in the Fontainebleau forest have shown mixed status: some reports indicate containment, while others report the fire is still spreading with 850 firefighters and 200 vehicles deployed. Authorities discovered ten ignition points and arrested two suspects on suspicion of arson.

On July 15, approximately 800 firefighters continued to tackle flare-ups in the Fontainebleau forest as French President Emmanuel Macron pledged to replant the historic forest. Meanwhile, authorities are investigating a volunteer firefighter as a suspect in starting the devastating blaze, which burned over 2,000 hectares near Paris.

logs.summary:
Ukraine struck additional warehouses of Russia's top online retailer Wildberries and intensified attacks on Ozon, causing economic disruption. In leadership moves, President Zelensky replaced the commander-in-chief with Mykhailo Drapatyi and fired Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, sparking protests. Meanwhile, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Russia's Lavrov in Manila, expressing readiness to help end the war but noting no quick deal is imminent.
Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Wildberries warehouses produced massive pillars of black smoke as fires raged at the facilities. Russia, stretched by Ukraine's drone attacks on its Black Sea Fleet, has pulled all warships from the Mediterranean Sea. Both sides have increased bridge strikes to disrupt resupply networks, indicating expectations of a prolonged stalemate, while the Kremlin warned against optimism on peace following the Rubio-Lavrov meeting.
The EU passed its 21st sanctions package with 218 new designations targeting Russia, including vessels that refuel shadow fleet tankers. Ukrainian strikes continued to hit Russian Wildberries warehouses, while new airstrikes caused deaths in both Ukraine and Russia, and a drone was shot down over NATO airspace.

logs.summary:
President Zelenskyy met with President Trump in Washington, discussing Ukraine producing its own powerful weapons and Patriot missile co-production, with Zelenskyy calling the talks productive. The US Senate overwhelmingly advanced a bipartisan Russia sanctions bill allowing tariffs on countries buying Russian oil. Ukraine struck an Iranian cargo ship in the Caspian Sea, claiming it carried drone/missile cargo for Russia, prompting Iranian threats of retaliation, while Europe fears more active Belarusian involvement in the conflict. Russia's Wildberries has paid 40 million in compensation for Ukrainian attacks, and a fuel crisis is gripping Russia with gas stations running out of fuel.
Ukraine's ongoing drone attacks on Russia's Wildberries online retailer have intensified and are now described as a key pressure point on Moscow's wartime economy. Following his visit to Washington, President Zelenskyy stated that Putin has "lost the initiative" as Ukraine's tech industry reshapes the conflict. Meanwhile, India continues to monitor threats to its seafarers in the Black Sea after a vessel near Chornomorsk port faced drone and missile dangers.
Russia shifted its propaganda narrative as losses mounted, while Ukraine struck two major Russian oil refineries shortly after President Zelenskyy's meeting with President Trump. Ukraine's foreign minister warned his Iranian counterpart against escalation after reports that Iran planned a ballistic missile strike on a Ukrainian port. Additionally, Zelenskyy and Netanyahu separately met with Trump at the White House and attended the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham.
Ukraine drone strikes targeted the Ryazan oil refinery and Wildberries logistics hubs on July 29, further pushing Russia's refining capacity to a 21-year low. A Ukrainian F-16 scored its first confirmed air-to-air kill against a Russian jet. The Indian Embassy is monitoring 13 Indian seafarers aboard the MV AMIR1 near Ukraine's Black Sea coast following safety concerns.

logs.summary:
The U.S. and Iran have paused attacks and resumed diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, with mediators reporting progress and talks focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, the Pentagon quietly removed four recent troop deaths from its official Iran war death toll, reclassifying them in a new category, sparking controversy. Additional concerns include the U.S.'s dangerously low weaponry supply and growing public skepticism over the war’s costs and duration.
Mediators reported that neither the U.S. nor Iran conducted any attacks for three consecutive days, signaling progress in ceasefire efforts. New polls indicate that only one in three Americans now support the war, the lowest reading since the conflict began, and a majority view it as going "very badly." The Pentagon continued to face scrutiny over its reclassification of four troop deaths from the conflict.

logs.summary:
Diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran have progressed, with Trump claiming "friendly" negotiations and Iran stating it controls the Strait of Hormuz. The House voted to restrict Trump's war powers amid growing opposition, and oil prices dropped over 2% on de-escalation hopes, while concerns persist over U.S. weapons stockpiles and the Pentagon's reclassification of casualty data.
Trump and Netanyahu held their first face-to-face meeting since launching the war, with Trump expressing frustrations with the Israeli leader beforehand. New polling shows support for the war has dropped to just one in three Americans, the lowest since the conflict began, while consumer confidence fell as gas prices resumed their climb. Iran stated it controls the Strait of Hormuz and is not seeking renewed talks, even as Trump claimed "good talks" were underway and threatened "very strong military action" if diplomacy fails.

news.headline: US-Iran War Live: Iran is pleading US to stop its naval blockade, Trump says
news.body: US-Iran War News Live Updates: US President Donald Trump on Monday said the United States was holding "good talks" with Iran and expressed hope that diplomacy could end the conflict, while warning that military strikes would resume if negotiations collapsed. Speaking aboard Air Force One, Trump said Tehran wanted talks because "we've been hitting them very hard" and added, "I think there's a good chance that something could happen... if it doesn't, we go back to doing what we were doing two days ago." His remarks came two days after Washington abruptly paused its two-week bombing campaign. However, the fragile calm was tested as Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Iraq reported drone attacks, while Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure. Iran denied seeking negotiations, with Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei calling such reports "fabricated" and insisting, "This is not in our DNA," though he confirmed indirect messages were still being exchanged through mediators. Tehran also maintained that it remained in control of the Strait of Hormuz, the crucial global oil shipping route at the centre of the crisis. Hopes that the pause could pave the way for diplomacy sent oil prices tumbling, with Brent crude plunging nearly 9% to around $88 a barrel after briefly crossing $100 last week. Reports suggested Trump halted the bombing campaign after military commanders warned of dwindling targets and concerns over ammunition supplies, claims the US president dismissed by insisting America had "a lot of ammunition" and was rapidly rebuilding its stockpiles. Despite the pause, uncertainty remains high as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz stays severely disrupted and both Washington and Tehran continue to disagree over future access to the strategic waterway. Follow IndiaToday.in for the latest updates.

logs.summary:
Iran launched a surprise missile attack on US forces in Jordan on July 28, which the US says it successfully intercepted, ending a five-day pause in the conflict. Diplomatic efforts continued with Oman presenting a Gulf-backed plan for voluntary fees to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran reportedly received Chinese shoulder-launched missile systems. The Pentagon faced renewed scrutiny over its reclassification of troop deaths, and public support for the war dropped to a new low of one in three Americans.
Iran rejected Oman's Gulf-backed proposal for joint management of the Strait of Hormuz, dashing hopes for a diplomatic resolution. The U.S. and Saudi Arabia launched joint strikes against Iran-aligned targets in Iraq, prompting a 5% spike in oil prices, while Jordan intercepted Iranian missiles aimed at Jordanian and U.S. forces. The Pentagon moved recent casualties into a new "Overseas Operations" category, and an analysis warns that recent fighting has further depleted U.S. air defense stockpiles.
Iran also struck three ships in the Strait of Hormuz during its missile attack on U.S. forces, expanding the theater of hostilities. Separately, reports indicate the cost of living in Iran has soared amid nearly five months of war, with consumer prices rising significantly. These developments add to the ongoing escalation and its economic toll.
Tensions escalated further as a US-owned gas tanker was set ablaze by a drone in Egypt, widening the theater of conflict. A new CNN poll showed President Trump losing ground ahead of the midterm elections amid the conflict, while analysts reported that US weapons stockpiles remain severely depleted with no end in sight. A detailed analysis of Iran's strategic calculus suggested the country chose to restart the fight to regain leverage after days of relative calm.

logs.summary:
New reports highlight that wildfires near Bordeaux are threatening key French defense-industrial sites including nuclear deterrence facilities and Rafale assembly plants. Meanwhile, emergency crews in Spain's Ávila and Madrid regions are racing to control blazes ahead of an approaching heatwave.
A record 63,000 people have been evacuated near Madrid as wildfires continue, while fire crews in Bordeaux brace for a 41°C (106°F) heatwave that threatens to reignite the blaze. The EU has warned that wildfire response must evolve due to climate change, and experts describe the recent blazes as signs of a new "mega fire" era with intensities like atomic bombs.
The European Union coordinates cross-border wildfire aid for France and Spain, deploying planes, helicopters, and ground units across 37 participating nations. First-person accounts from the fire zone describe the extraordinary intensity of the blazes, while fire crews continue to battle the massive wildfire near Bordeaux as temperatures exceed 40°C.

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

logs.summary:
As of July 29, the confirmed death toll has risen to 13, with the Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi reporting the fatalities, including two women found in the collapsed Aeon Mall and others elsewhere in Kumamoto Prefecture. Rescue operations by Japan's Self-Defense Forces continue at the shopping mall and damaged sites, with many people still missing and over 50 injured. Additional damage includes a collapsed chimney at a Nippon Paper Industries factory, a train derailment, and fires triggered by the quake.
Search and rescue operations continue in Kumamoto Prefecture following the July 28 earthquake. While many reports still cite a death toll of 13, one source now reports the toll has risen to at least 18 as rescuers comb through rubble at a collapsed mall and damaged homes.
As of July 29, the death toll from the earthquake has been confirmed at 18 by multiple sources, including a foreign national, as rescue operations continue at the collapsed Aeon Mall and damaged homes. Geological analysis indicates the Hinagu fault zone, which caused a 2016 quake, likely triggered this temblor.
Rescue operations continue with the death toll confirmed at 18, but new reports indicate that Toyota and other auto and chip manufacturers have halted production at plants in Kyushu due to supply chain disruptions caused by the earthquake. The economic impact is emerging as a significant secondary effect of the disaster.
